summary: GL-101 and GL-204 are both Approved glossary entries titled 'Settlement Date' but they define it differently. GL-101 (v1.0, owner Avery Example (SYNTHETIC)) defines it as the date on which cash and securities are actually exchanged to complete a trade (an actual/occurrence date). GL-204 (v2.1, owner Blake Example (SYNTHETIC)) defines it as the contractual date by which payment and delivery must complete, as agreed at execution (an agreed/due date). These are not equivalent: the actual exchange date can differ from the contractual due date (for example on a late or failed settlement). The glossary also records a possible_duplicate link between the two entries, and they disagree on the recorded CDE flag (GL-101 true, GL-204 false). Because two Approved internal sources conflict, I have not picked one; a draft reconciliation is offered for Data Steward review only and the matter is escalated.

conflicts_identified: Definitional conflict: GL-101 (v1.0, Approved) defines Settlement Date as the date cash and securities are exchanged to complete a trade; GL-204 (v2.1, Approved) defines it as the contractual date by which payment and delivery must complete, as agreed at execution. One describes when settlement occurs, the other when it is due; they can differ in practice. Both are surfaced; neither is chosen.

CDE flag inconsistency: GL-101 has recorded_cde_flag true while GL-204 has recorded_cde_flag false, for what is nominally the same term. The glossary alone does not show which, if either, is correct, and no CDE-criteria policy document has been provided.

Duplicate-term status: the glossary holds a term link GL-101 -> GL-204 with relation possible_duplicate, i.e. the glossary itself flags them as a possible duplicate, but both remain Approved under different owners and different versions.
Ownership/version divergence: different owners (Avery Example (SYNTHETIC) vs Blake Example (SYNTHETIC)) and versions (1.0 vs 2.1) with no recorded precedence between them.
